flashcard_questions.q: The process of introducing a small quantity of dead or inactive pathogen into the body to stimulate the immune system to produce antibodies, providing future protection against that disease.
Unique proteins on the surface of a pathogen that the immune system recognises as foreign, triggering an immune response.
Proteins produced by white blood cells (lymphocytes) that bind to specific antigens on pathogens, marking them for destruction or neutralising them directly.

flashcard_questions.a: Medicines that kill or prevent the growth of bacteria inside the body without damaging human cells. They have no effect on viruses.
Protection that comes when most of a population is immune, so the pathogen cannot easily spread to people who are not immune.
